inspiration: Talent nodes come in a small family of faceted shapes (diamond, hexagon, octagon, half-octagon) at two sizes; the shape carries the tier. An artist could make a family of distinct faceted node shapes for ability tiers (Blizzard_SharedTalentUI masks).

Sound alerts are grouped by category, and each category holds short named cues with text labels (Blizzard_CooldownViewer/CooldownViewerSoundAlertData.lua). A grouped cue picker is a clean alert pattern.
Tutorial callouts use a few distance bands defined in one data table (Blizzard_BoostTutorial/Blizzard_TutorialRacialData.lua). Distance-tier callouts help players read range.
Housing and edit-mode data providers show sample icons while the player places HUD parts (Blizzard_FrameXMLUtil/EditModeAuraDataProvider.lua). A placement-mode preview idea for our hud-ui.
The map event overlay is a separate data provider on top of the base map (Blizzard_WorldMap/WM_EventOverlayDataProvider.lua). Layered map overlays suit zone heat or event tint.
The XML schema enumerates frame anchor points (Blizzard_SharedXML/UI.xsd). A declarative layout schema could keep our HUD positions data-driven.

briefs.label: Faceted talent node family
briefs.why: Tier reads at a glance from the node silhouette, before the player reads any text.
briefs.keep: a small family of geometric node silhouettes (diamond, hexagon, octagon); one shape per tier; two node sizes
briefs.change: our own faceting angles and corner cuts; a keystone shape that is not a polygon; a glyph row on the node edge

briefs.label: Grouped cue picker
briefs.why: Alert sounds stay learnable when they are grouped into a few named categories, each with a text label.
briefs.keep: categories with a short list of named cues, text label next to each cue, one category at a time
briefs.change: our own cue sounds (synth stingers, not animal calls); categories by weapon class or school, not by animal

briefs.label: Distance-tier callouts
briefs.why: A short, medium and long range band lets a hint fire at the right distance without a hard-coded radius per case.
briefs.keep: a single table of named range tiers; callouts keyed to the tier; a tutorial hook per tier
briefs.change: our own radius values in metres or tiles of our own grid; tier names from our fiction; an icon per tier instead of text

briefs.label: Placement-mode HUD preview
briefs.why: Showing sample icons while the player moves HUD parts lets them place things without a live fight.
briefs.keep: sample data feeds the preview; placement mode is a separate state from play; icons, not text, in the preview
briefs.change: our own sample set (a sample shield bar, a sample cooldown ring); a ghost layer sized for 375 px wide phones; snap to the thumb zone

briefs.label: Layered zone event overlay
briefs.why: Events drawn as an overlay layer on the base map keep the map readable and let the layer toggle on and off.
briefs.keep: base map and event overlay as separate providers; overlay on top of the base map; toggleable layer
briefs.change: our overlay as zone heat or colour tint rather than icons; a time-decay on the tint; our own layer names
